fact_verdicts.note: Cherokee County KS NPL page, Jan 2023 update (page updated Dec 8, 2025): 'If new residential development is identified within the site boundary, EPA will test the residential yards'.

Page says 'The OU5 remedy does not address the potential future residential development of the area.' and ICs 'limit land use on capped waste areas' (OU3/4/6). 'Limits reuse of OU5 for housing' is the researcher's inference.

Cherokee entry: 'The 12-acre Work Area #1 ... used by the landowner for farming cash crops like wheat and soybeans.' 'More than 2,700 acres ... restored as agricultural, livestock use and wildlife habitat.' 'Last updated September 2019'.
'The counties and ports plan to develop industrial areas on the 9,511 acres the CDA now own'; ceremony Wed July 12, 2023; CDA ownership 'back in March'. Scope: whole depot; lagoons not mentioned.

Sep 29, 2022: 'The CDA at long last is about to become the owner of the former Umatilla Chemical Depot'; 'nearly 10,000 acres'; director on being 'strategic and thoughtful'. Whole depot; lagoons not mentioned.

Mar 30, 2023: 'Obsidian's map showed the depot as its Oregon hub'; Obsidian (Lake Oswego solar) applied to DOE Nov 2022; PNW Hydrogen Association applied; no hub acreage given. Whole depot; no lagoons.

2024 award; 'The authority designated 5,500 acres of this land as a wildlife refuge'; Tribes received title to 4,000 acres, 'an important cultural site'. EPA names the Umatilla Army Depot Superfund site; no lagoons mention.

Signed Nov 27, 2017 by Oregon Adjutant General and USACE: 'dedicates 7,500 acres of the former depot's 19,729 acres as a new Oregon National Guard Training Center'; posted Jan 11, 2018. Whole depot; no lagoons.
